cards.text: Jesus is still on the Mount of Olives, answering His disciples about the end of the age. Now He gives them something to watch for: "the abomination of desolation," spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place. Then comes a quick note right in the middle: let the reader understand.

cards.question: When they see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place, Jesus says those in Judea should flee to the ___.

cards.text: There's NO time to pack. Whoever's up on the housetop shouldn't even come down to grab anything from the house, and friend, I'm the guy who goes back in three times for my keys.

cards.question: Jesus says the person out working in the field can run home for their cloak first.
With everyone running for the mountains, Jesus says, "How miserable those days will be" for which people?

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them to pray about when that run will happen.

cards.question: Jesus tells them to pray that their flight to the mountains won't happen in which season?

cards.text: Not in winter, and not on the Sabbath either. Then Jesus says why: at that time there will be great tribulation.

cards.question: Jesus says a tribulation like this one has never been seen since the beginning of the world.

cards.text: That's heavy, friend. But Jesus isn't finished, and the next thing He says is about the elect.

cards.question: Jesus says that if those days of tribulation went on as they were, nobody would be saved. What happens to those days for the sake of the elect?

cards.text: Then Jesus warns them about what people will say at that time: 'Look, here is the Christ!' or 'There He is!'

cards.question: When someone says, "Look, here is the Christ!" what does Jesus tell His disciples to do?

cards.text: Here's why: false Christs and false prophets will appear. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer believing an expired coupon that SWORE it was still good, so I'm listening REAL close to this part.

cards.question: Jesus says these false Christs and false prophets will perform great signs and wonders.
Jesus says the false Christs and false prophets will try to deceive someone, if that were possible. Who?

cards.text: Jesus says, "See, I have told you in advance." So if anyone says He's out in the wilderness, don't go, and if they say He's in the inner rooms, don't believe it.

cards.question: Instead, Jesus says the coming of the Son of Man will be like something that comes from the east and flashes as far as the west. What is it?

cards.text: Lightning doesn't need a group chat to announce it, friend. Then Jesus adds a short saying: "Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather."
Then Jesus says what comes immediately after the tribulation of those days: the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.

cards.question: With the sun darkened and the moon giving no light, Jesus says the stars will ___ from the sky.

cards.text: And the powers of the heavens will be shaken. At that time, the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven.

cards.question: When the sign of the Son of Man appears in heaven, Jesus says all the tribes of the earth will ___.
Then all the tribes of the earth will see the Son of Man coming. How does Jesus say He will come?

cards.text: With power and great glory, friend. And then comes a loud trumpet call.

cards.question: With a loud trumpet call, who does the Son of Man send out?
Jesus says the angels will gather His elect from only one place on earth.

cards.text: Now Jesus gives them a lesson from the fig tree. I read my oven the same way: the smell ALWAYS shows up before the timer dings.

cards.question: When the fig tree's branches turn tender and sprout leaves, what does Jesus say you know is near?
Jesus says it's the same with "all these things." When they see them, how near does He say He is?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened."

cards.question: Jesus says heaven and earth will pass away, but His ___ will never pass away.

cards.text: Heaven and earth can go, and His words are still standing. And friend, Jesus isn't done teaching on that mountain yet, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 3 quotes "all these things.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage: Jesus is on the Mount of Olives, answering His disciples about the end of the age. These come from Matthew 24:3, but the card cites only Matthew 24:15 and gives no reference for them.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "With everyone running for the mountains" stretches the text. Matthew 24:16 tells only "those who are in Judea" to flee, not everyone.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card tells almost none of the passage. "That's heavy, friend" and a teaser that the next line is about the elect only stall before card 11, which carries all of verse 22. The setup should tell part of verse 22, such as that nobody would be saved if those days continued.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Verse 23 is conditional: "if anyone says to you." The card turns it into a certainty: "what people will say." The card drops the "if."

The setup says Jesus "warns them" about these claims. That gives away the answer to card 2 ("Do not believe it") and rules out the wrong answers ("Go and see for themselves" and "Ask the priests about it").

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason that the tribes of the earth will mourn rather than rejoice or sing when the sign of the Son of Man appears. The pick comes down to luck. Also, the two wrong answers mean nearly the same thing, so the right answer stands out as the odd one. The setup needs more context, or the card should ask a different question.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The joke "I read my oven the same way" compares itself to a lesson the baker hasn't heard yet. The fig tree's sign (tender branches and leaves mean summer is near) only comes on card 2. With no setup, "the same way" doesn't click.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
